description: Original, non-executable platform guidance for iOS, Android, desktop, and unmodeled project kinds. All outcomes are manual or unsupported.

scenarios.summary: This Windows host cannot provide the native iOS build toolchain. A macOS host with a mutually compatible macOS and Xcode release is required.
manual_steps: Keep the requested iOS outcome in the plan and report that native compilation is unavailable on this host.
Ask the project owner to select a supported macOS build host before planning native compilation.
Do not substitute an Android build, accept Apple terms, sign an app, or provision a device as an automatic workaround.
readiness_constraints: The local platform predicate is Windows; no compatible macOS host or Xcode SDK was observed.
This scenario is unsupported for native iOS compilation and cannot be changed to ready by installing a Windows SDK.
No remote build service, Apple account, signing identity, or device is assumed.
scenarios.verification: Before native iOS compilation, confirm the participant-selected macOS host and Xcode release pair against Apple’s current support matrix; retain unsupported status until that host is qualified.

scenarios.summary: This Linux host cannot provide the native iOS build toolchain. A macOS host with a mutually compatible macOS and Xcode release is required.
manual_steps: Keep the requested iOS outcome in the plan and report that native compilation is unavailable on this host.
Ask the project owner to select a supported macOS build host before planning native compilation.
Do not substitute an Android build, accept Apple terms, sign an app, or provision a device as an automatic workaround.
readiness_constraints: The local platform predicate is Linux; no compatible macOS host or Xcode SDK was observed.
This scenario is unsupported for native iOS compilation and cannot be changed to ready by installing a Linux SDK.
No remote build service, Apple account, signing identity, or device is assumed.
scenarios.verification: Before native iOS compilation, confirm the participant-selected macOS host and Xcode release pair against Apple’s current support matrix; retain unsupported status until that host is qualified.

scenarios.summary: A Mac can host native iOS development, but Xcode and Apple SDK use, signing, and device setup require participant review and are not qualified here.
manual_steps: Preserve the project’s declared Xcode, Swift, deployment target, and package versions; first check whether an existing toolchain already satisfies them.
Choose an Xcode release compatible with the known macOS version and target SDK by consulting Apple’s current support matrix.
Review and accept Xcode and Apple SDK terms personally before any installation or use; do not accept terms automatically.
Review disk space and any restart notice for the chosen release; separately authorize any Apple account, signing, or device provisioning.
readiness_constraints: Apple’s supported macOS versions vary by Xcode release; an unknown macOS version remains manual and unmet.
The reviewed Xcode requirements matrix does not establish one fixed disk-space or restart requirement for every release; check the selected release before manual setup.
No license acceptance, SDK installation, account setup, signing, device provisioning, or native runtime test occurred.
scenarios.verification: A participant must confirm the chosen Xcode/macOS/SDK combination in Apple’s current matrix and separately verify the target SDK and signing or device requirements; no native qualification is asserted.

scenarios.summary: Android development may use Android Studio or a project-matched SDK, but host requirements, SDK package selection, license acceptance, emulator capacity, and devices need participant review.
manual_steps: Preserve project-declared JDK, Gradle, Android Gradle Plugin, SDK, and NDK versions; check existing installations before proposing changes.

Confirm the host meets the current Android Studio requirements: macOS 12 or later with supported Mac CPU, Windows 10 64-bit, or 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.31 or later and a supported desktop environment.

Check available storage before any participant-approved setup: Android Studio alone lists 8 GB minimum; Studio with an emulator lists 16 GB, and each additional virtual device may need up to 6 GB more.
Review and accept each applicable Android SDK package license personally before use; do not accept licenses or download SDK packages automatically.
Choose a physical device or emulator only after separately reviewing project needs, hardware/virtualization support, account access, and device authorization.
readiness_constraints: The platform predicate gives OS and architecture only; CPU microarchitecture, virtualization, memory, free disk space, and the project’s exact SDK versions remain unverified.
Current Android Studio guidance lists at least 8 GB free space for Studio and 16 GB for Studio plus an emulator; emulator images and additional virtual devices add storage.
No reboot requirement is established by this descriptor; if a later vendor installation requests a restart, the participant must review and schedule it.
No SDK license was accepted, SDK or emulator package was downloaded, account was configured, device was provisioned, or native build was qualified.
scenarios.verification: Before a participant-approved Android setup, verify the current vendor requirements and project-declared SDK/JDK/Gradle versions, confirm free storage and any emulator prerequisites, and record each license decision; keep readiness manual until the selected target is actually checked.

scenarios.summary: Current Android Studio requirements do not support Windows ARM hosts or Linux ARM hosts; this descriptor cannot claim Android Studio readiness for those platforms.
manual_steps: Preserve the Android project goal and report that the current Android Studio host is unsupported.
Ask the project owner to choose a vendor-supported host or separately reviewed development approach before changing project tooling.
Do not treat a manual SDK download, emulator, remote host, or alternative IDE as available without separate evidence and participant approval.
readiness_constraints: Android Developers currently marks Windows ARM and Linux ARM machines as unsupported for Android Studio.
The host is unsupported for this Android Studio guidance even if other OS/architecture details are known; do not report it ready.
No alternative IDE, CLI SDK support, remote service, emulator, or runtime qualification is asserted.
scenarios.verification: Recheck Android Developers’ current system requirements for the exact host architecture before selecting any alternative; retain unsupported status until a supported approach is established and qualified.

scenarios.summary: Desktop projects vary by language, target OS, packaging format, native dependencies, and signing needs; the project kind alone is not enough to select an SDK or installer.
manual_steps: Preserve the requested desktop target and record its language, runtime, target operating systems, architecture, packaging format, and existing build-tool versions.
Ask the project owner to identify required platform SDKs, native libraries, code-signing, store accounts, and distribution constraints before proposing setup.
Review each selected vendor license personally and check storage, privilege, and restart effects before any separately approved setup.
Keep unknown requirements visible as manual actions; do not run project scripts, provision signing identities, or alter package and lock files.
readiness_constraints: The generic desktop project kind does not identify an SDK, runtime, packaging method, or target OS.
Architecture, storage needs, license requirements, and any reboot requirement depend on the chosen project-specific toolchain and are not inferred.
No native desktop toolchain or packaging flow was installed or qualified.
scenarios.verification: Confirm the target operating systems and architecture with the project owner, then verify each project-declared toolchain and vendor requirement before changing the machine or project.

scenarios.summary: The project kind is not modeled by a reviewed catalog path. Preserve the requested outcome and continue with partial readiness while gathering only the missing platform and toolchain facts.
manual_steps: Keep the user’s stated goal unchanged and summarize which project facts remain unknown.
Ask for the language or framework, target operating systems and architecture, current toolchain versions, and any install or license constraints.
Offer a bounded manual next step based on those facts after review; do not assume an SDK, installer, command, account, or device is available.
readiness_constraints: No catalog model for this project kind was selected; unknown does not mean supported or ready.
No commands, URLs, paths, installs, license acceptance, or project changes are generated from this descriptor.
Interview and planning may continue with partial readiness and explicit unresolved questions.
scenarios.verification: Verify the gathered project kind, toolchain declarations, target platforms, and constraints with the project owner before proposing any specific recipe or exercise.
